reviewed_use_clause.text: [L1] The deformation to the normal cone gives the open flat deformation family $D_i\to\mathbb P^1$ with special fibre the normal cone and ordinary fibres the ambient scheme and a well-defined specialization operation on Chow groups, natural in the base ([[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]]).

reviewed_use_clause.text: [F1] For a product $G$ of complex general linear groups, equivariant Borel–Moore homology is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j])$; its normalized dualizing object restricts to the ordinary one, and the groups agree in the stable range with dimension-shifted Borel approximations. The case $G=T=(\mathrm{GL}_1)^r$ applies. [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]

[F3] Assume AC. The definition [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] fixes $H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j])$, its stable Borel value $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2b}(X\times_GU;k)$ for a free smooth approximation with $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, and the corner degrees $d_i+d_j-p$; the ambient category is that of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].

[F2] [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] fixes the source-first convention, the geometric product $a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^!(a\boxtimes b)$ with its degree drop $2d_j$, the ordered coordinates, the zero rule for nonmatching indices and the corner degrees.

reviewed_use_clause.text: [A8] For a complex measure $\nu$, $\mu\mapsto\int h\,d\mu$ is linear in $\mu$ and $\int\mathbf 1_B\,d\mu=\mu(B)$; and $E_x=\mu_{x,x}$ below is a regular measure because it is the representing measure of a bounded functional on $C(K;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]], [[def-complex-measure]]).

reviewed_use_clause.text: [F5] For $X=\mathbb P^n_k$ and every integer $d$ and every $q$ the evaluation pairing $H^q(X,\mathcal O(d))\times H^{n-q}(X,\mathcal O(-d-n-1))\to k$, $(\alpha,\eta)\mapsto t_X(\alpha\cup\eta)$, formed with the cup product for $\mathcal O(d)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathcal O(-d-n-1)\to\omega_X$, is a perfect pairing; for $q=0$ and $d\ge0$ it is the residue pairing of monomials, i.e. the coefficient of $(x_0\cdots x_n)^{-1}$, and it is compatible with multiplication by homogeneous polynomials. ([[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]], [[lem-projective-space-top-cohomology-residue-pairing]], [[def-cup-product-sheaf-cohomology]])

[F3] For $n\ge1$ and $d\ge0$ the pairing $H^0(\mathbb P^n_k,\mathcal O(d))\times H^n(\mathbb P^n_k,\mathcal O(-n-1-d))\to k$ given by the cup product for $\mathcal O(d)\otimes\mathcal O(-n-1-d)\to\mathcal O(-n-1)$ followed by $t_{\mathbb P^n}$, equivalently by the coefficient of $(x_0\cdots x_n)^{-1}$ in the product of monomials, is a perfect $k$-bilinear pairing, compatible with multiplication by homogeneous polynomials; for $n=0$ it is ordinary multiplication $k\times k\to k$. ([[lem-projective-space-top-cohomology-residue-pairing]])
